Also "Append findings to docs/reviews.md" — but I have no write tool! read/glob/grep are read-only. Hmm. The skill tool, subagent... Maybe subagents can write files. The main tools listed: experimental_image_generate, glob, grep, read, skill, subagent, execute. No write. So to append to docs/reviews.md I'll need a subagent with write access (09-documentation or general or 10-git). Hmm, that's awkward but workable: I compose the review text, then ask a subagent to append it verbatim to docs/reviews.md.

Plan:
1. Static review: read all scoped files, grep for issues, check contracts 1-8, 10 statically.
2. Delegate gate running (contract 9 + git status/diffs) to a general subagent (or multiple in parallel). Ask it to report raw outputs: vitest summary (files/tests counts), typecheck output, build result, pytest summary, engine verify output (incl sha256), git status --short, and git diff --stat for the scoped files plus README/devpost/decisions.

The main tools listed: experimental_image_generate, glob, grep, read, skill, subagent, execute. No write. So to append to docs/reviews.md I'll need a subagent with write access (09-documentation or general or 10-git). Hmm, that's awkward but workable: I compose the review text, then ask a subagent to append it verbatim to docs/reviews.md.

1: /**
2:  * The district name join for the cartogram (Phase E5 map). districts.csv
3:  * and the map geometry come from two different publishers: the CSV spells
4:  * names in plain ASCII with Czech administrative prefixes intact, while
5:  * the geoBoundaries outlines ship proper diacritics and, for the nine
6:  * city and direction units, English wording. One normalizer turns both
7:  * sides into the same key, so the cartogram can shade an outline from a
8:  * CSV row without a hand maintained crosswalk table and without any
9:  * network at runtime.
10:  *
11:  * The rules, in order: strip combining marks, lowercase, collapse every
12:  * run of punctuation to a single space, drop leading capital prefixes
13:  * (only while tokens remain to drop, so Plzen mesto keeps its mesto),
14:  * and finally read a lone n as the word nad. The alias table maps the
15:  * nine English spellings onto the Czech wording the CSV uses.
16:  */
17: 
18: /** Leading tokens the Czech capital and city prefixes decompose to. */
19: const CAPITAL_PREFIXES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['hl', 'hlavni', 'mesto', 'm'])
20: 
21: /**
22:  * geoBoundaries ships English names for the nine units the CSV spells in
23:  * Czech, keyed by the normalized English form.
24:  */
25: const ENGLISH_ALIASES: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
26:   prague: 'praha',
27:   'prague east': 'praha vychod',
28:   'prague west': 'praha zapad',
29:   'plzen city': 'plzen mesto',
30:   'plzen north': 'plzen sever',
31:   'plzen south': 'plzen jih',
32:   'brno city': 'brno mesto',
33:   'brno country': 'brno venkov',
34:   'ostrava city': 'ostrava mesto',
35: }
36: 
37: /** One district name reduced to its comparison key. */
38: export function normalizeDistrictName(name: string): string {
39:   const plain = name
40:     .normalize('NFD')
41:     .replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, '')
42:     .toLowerCase()
43:   const tokens = plain.split(/[^a-z0-9]+/).filter((token) => token.length > 0)
44: 
45:   let start = 0
46:   while (start < tokens.length - 1 && CAPITAL_PREFIXES.has(tokens[start] ?? '')) {
47:     start += 1
48:   }
49: 
50:   return tokens
51:     .slice(start)
52:     .map((token) => (token === 'n' ? 'nad' : token))
53:     .join(' ')
54: }
55: 
56: /** The join key: the normalized name, then the English alias table. */
57: export function districtKey(name: string): string {
58:   const key = normalizeDistrictName(name)
59:   return ENGLISH_ALIASES[key] ?? key
60: }

117: interface Prose {
118:   file: string
119:   line: number
120:   chunk: string
121:   where: string

124: function lineOf(text: string, index: number): number {
125:   return text.slice(0, index).split('\n').length
126: }

128: /** Pull every piece of prose out of one source file. */
129: function proseOf(file: string, text: string): Prose[] {
130:   const prose: Prose[] = []
131:   // Mask URL scheme separators first: "https://" inside a string would
132:   // otherwise read as a line comment and eat the closing quote or
133:   // backtick, shifting every later string match and reporting code as
134:   // prose (the GEMINI_URL template in src/lib/shockParse.ts exposed
135:   // this). The mask keeps the character count so line numbers hold.
136:   const URL_MASK = '\u0000\u0000\u0000'
137:   let rest = text.split('://').join(URL_MASK)
138: 
139:   const push = (chunk: string, index: number, where: string): void => {
140:     prose.push({
141:       file,
142:       line: lineOf(text, index),
143:       chunk: chunk.split(URL_MASK).join('://'),
144:       where,
145:     })
146:   }
147: 
148:   // Block comments first, then line comments, so an apostrophe inside a
149:   // comment can never open a string that swallows real code.
150:   rest = rest.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, (chunk, index: number) => {
151:     push(chunk, index, 'block comment')
152:     return ' '
153:   })
154:   rest = rest.replace(/\/\/[^\n]*/g, (chunk, index: number) => {
155:     push(chunk, index, 'line comment')
156:     return ' '
157:   })
158: 
159:   const stringPattern = /'(?:[^'\\\n]|\\.)*'|"(?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*"|`(?:[^`\\]|\\.)*`/g
160:   let match: RegExpExecArray | null
161:   while ((match = stringPattern.exec(rest)) !== null) {
162:     // Template expressions are code, not copy.
163:     const chunk = match[0].replace(/\$\{[^}]*\}/g, '')
164:     push(chunk, match.index, 'string literal')
165:   }
166:   rest = rest.replace(stringPattern, ' ')
167: 
168:   // JSX text nodes: prose between a tag close and the next tag open.
169:   const jsxPattern = />([^<>{}]+)</g
170:   while ((match = jsxPattern.exec(rest)) !== null) {
171:     const chunk = match[1] ?? ''
172:     if (PROSE.test(chunk) && /[A-Za-z]/.test(chunk)) {
173:       push(chunk, match.index, 'jsx text')
174:     }
175:   }
176: 
177:   return prose
178: }

182:   if (chunk.includes(EM_DASH)) {
183:     problems.push('em dash')
184:   }
185:   if (chunk.includes(EN_DASH)) {
186:     problems.push('en dash')
187:   }
188:   if (chunk.includes(MINUS_SIGN)) {
189:     problems.push('minus sign')
190:   }
191:   if (chunk.includes(DOUBLE_HYPHEN)) {
192:     problems.push('double hyphen')
193:   }
194:   if (chunk.includes(SPACED_HYPHEN)) {
195:     problems.push('spaced hyphen')
196:   }
197:   return problems
198: }

1: """Regenerate src/assets/czechia-districts.ts from the geoBoundaries release.
2: 
3: The cartogram map needs one SVG path per Czech district, and the app must
4: never fetch geometry at runtime, so the outlines are baked into a TypeScript
5: module that Vite bundles. This script is the build time step: it reads the
6: downloaded GeoJSON, projects it onto a flat map, simplifies it with
7: Douglas Peucker, rounds it onto an integer grid, and writes the module.
8: 
9: Source (public domain, fetched once when the geometry was committed):
10: 
11:   https://www.geoboundaries.org/api/current/gbOpen/CZE/ADM2/
12:   https://github.com/wmgeolab/geoBoundaries/raw/9469f09/releaseData/gbOpen/CZE/ADM2/geoBoundaries-CZE-ADM2_simplified.geojson
13: 
14: Download it with curl, then run:
15: 
16:   python3 scripts/map/build_district_geometry.py cze-adm2-simplified.geojson
17: 
18: The name rules live in src/lib/districtNames.ts, and
19: src/lib/districtNames.test.ts pins the join against data/tangerine/districts.csv,
20: so a regeneration that loses a district fails the TypeScript suite.
21: """
22: 
23: from __future__ import annotations
24: 
25: import json
26: import math
27: import re
28: import sys
29: import unicodedata
30: from pathlib import Path
31: 
32: REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
33: DEFAULT_INPUT = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path("cze-adm2-simplified.geojson")
34: DEFAULT_OUTPUT = REPO / "src" / "assets" / "czechia-districts.ts"
35: 
36: # Douglas Peucker tolerance in projected degrees. At the shipped scale one
37: # unit of the 1000 wide viewBox is under a pixel, and 0.0025 degrees is
38: # roughly half a pixel, so the simplification is invisible on screen.
39: TOLERANCE = 0.0025
40: 
41: VIEW_WIDTH = 1000
42: BORDER = 6.0
43: 
44: # geoBoundaries spells nine city and direction units in English while
45: # data/tangerine/districts.csv spells them in Czech. Keyed by the
46: # normalized English form, mirroring ENGLISH_ALIASES in districtNames.ts.
47: ALIASES = {
48:     "prague": "praha",
49:     "prague east": "praha vychod",
50:     "prague west": "praha zapad",
51:     "plzen city": "plzen mesto",
52:     "plzen north": "plzen sever",
53:     "plzen south": "plzen jih",
54:     "brno city": "brno mesto",
55:     "brno country": "brno venkov",
56:     "ostrava city": "ostrava mesto",
57: }
58: 
59: CAPITAL_PREFIXES = {"hl", "hlavni", "mesto", "m"}
60: 
61: 
62: def rings_of(geometry: dict) -> list:
63:     """Every ring of a Polygon or MultiPolygon feature."""
64:     if geometry["type"] == "Polygon":
65:         return geometry["coordinates"]
66:     rings: list = []
67:     for polygon in geometry["coordinates"]:
68:         rings.extend(polygon)
69:     return rings
70: 
71: 
72: def project(lon: float, lat: float, lat0: float, lon0: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
73:     """Equirectangular with a cosine correction, y pointing down."""
74:     return ((lon - lon0) * math.cos(math.radians(lat0)), -lat)
75: 
76: 
77: def simplify(points: list, tolerance: float) -> list:
78:     """Iterative Douglas Peucker over a closed ring (first point repeated)."""
79:     if len(points) < 5:
80:         return points
81:     keep = [False] * len(points)
82:     keep[0] = keep[-1] = True
83:     stack = [(0, len(points) - 1)]
84:     tolerance_sq = tolerance * tolerance
85:     while stack:
86:         start, end = stack.pop()
87:         if end <= start + 1:
88:             continue
89:         ax, ay = points[start]
90:         bx, by = points[end]
91:         dx, dy = bx - ax, by - ay
92:         norm = dx * dx + dy * dy
93:         best = -1.0
94:         best_index = -1
95:         for index in range(start + 1, end):
96:             px, py = points[index]
97:             if norm == 0:
98:                 distance = (px - ax) ** 2 + (py - ay) ** 2
99:             else:
100:                 t = ((px - ax) * dx + (py - ay) * dy) / norm
101:                 t = 0.0 if t < 0 else (1.0 if t > 1 else t)
102:                 distance = (px - (ax + t * dx)) ** 2 + (py - (ay + t * dy)) ** 2
103:             if distance > best:
104:                 best = distance
105:                 best_index = index
106:         if best > tolerance_sq and best_index > 0:
107:             keep[best_index] = True
108:             stack.append((start, best_index))
109:             stack.append((best_index, end))
110:     return [point for point, flagged in zip(points, keep) if flagged]
111: 
112: 
113: def district_key(name: str) -> str:
114:     """The same join key src/lib/districtNames.ts produces."""
115:     plain = "".join(
116:         character
117:         for character in unicodedata.normalize("NFD", name)
118:         if not unicodedata.combining(character)
119:     )
120:     tokens = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", " ", plain.lower()).strip().split()
121:     start = 0
122:     while start < len(tokens) - 1 and tokens[start] in CAPITAL_PREFIXES:
123:         start += 1
124:     key = " ".join("nad" if token == "n" else token for token in tokens[start:])
125:     return ALIASES.get(key, key)
126: 
127: 
128: def main() -> None:
129:     document = json.loads(DEFAULT_INPUT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
130: 
131:     latitudes: list[float] = []
132:     longitudes: list[float] = []
133:     for feature in document["features"]:
134:         for ring in rings_of(feature["geometry"]):
135:             for lon, lat in ring:
136:                 longitudes.append(lon)
137:                 latitudes.append(lat)
138:     lat0 = (min(latitudes) + max(latitudes)) / 2
139:     lon0 = (min(longitudes) + max(longitudes)) / 2
140: 
141:     projected: list[tuple[str, list[list[tuple[float, float]]]]] = []
142:     for feature in document["features"]:
143:         shape: list[list[tuple[float, float]]] = []
144:         for ring in rings_of(feature["geometry"]):
145:             points = [project(lon, lat, lat0, lon0) for lon, lat in ring]
146:             points = simplify(points, TOLERANCE)
147:             if len(points) >= 4:
148:                 shape.append(points)
149:         projected.append((feature["properties"]["shapeName"], shape))
150: 
151:     xs = [x for _, shape in projected for ring in shape for x, _ in ring]
152:     ys = [y for _, shape in projected for ring in shape for _, y in ring]
153:     min_x, max_x = min(xs), max(xs)
154:     min_y, max_y = min(ys), max(ys)
155: 
156:     span_x = max_x - min_x
157:     span_y = max_y - min_y
158:     height = round(VIEW_WIDTH * span_y / span_x)
159:     scale = (VIEW_WIDTH - 2 * BORDER) / span_x
160: 
161:     def emit(ring: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> str:
162:         steps = [
163:             f"{round((x - min_x) * scale + BORDER)} {round((y - min_y) * scale + BORDER)}"
164:             for x, y in ring
165:         ]
166:         return "M" + "L".join(steps) + "Z"
167: 
168:     rows: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
169:     points_total = 0
170:     for name, shape in projected:
171:         path = "".join(emit(ring) for ring in shape)
172:         points_total += sum(len(ring) for ring in shape)
173:         rows.append((district_key(name), path))
174: 
175:     keys = [key for key, _ in rows]
176:     duplicates = sorted({key for key in keys if keys.count(key) > 1})
177:     if duplicates:
178:         raise SystemExit(f"duplicate normalized keys: {duplicates}")
179: 
180:     body = "\n".join(f"  {{ name: '{key}', path: '{path}' }}," for key, path in rows)
181:     module = f"""/**
182:  * Simplified district geometry for the cartogram map, written by
183:  * scripts/map/build_district_geometry.py from geoBoundaries gbOpen
184:  * CZE ADM2 (Public Domain, www.geoboundaries.org, 77 districts). The
185:  * outlines are projected to a flat map, simplified with Douglas
186:  * Peucker, and rounded onto a 1000 by {height} integer grid so the map
187:  * keeps the same chunky pixel edge the rest of the station wears.
188:  * Names are normalized keys, the same shape src/lib/districtNames.ts
189:  * produces, so the cartogram joins a districts.csv row to its outline
190:  * with no network at runtime.
191:  */
192: 
193: /** The viewBox every path in this file is drawn on. */
194: export const CZECHIA_VIEW_BOX = '0 0 1000 {height}'
195: 
196: /** One district outline under its normalized name. */
197: export interface DistrictGeometry {{
198:   /** Normalized district name, the join key. */
199:   name: string
200:   /** SVG path data on CZECHIA_VIEW_BOX. */
201:   path: string
202: }}
203: 
204: /** All 77 districts, one path each. */
205: export const CZECHIA_DISTRICTS: readonly DistrictGeometry[] = [
206: {body}
207: ]
208: 
209: /** Guard against a truncated or overgrown asset. */
210: export const CZECHIA_DISTRICT_COUNT = {len(rows)}
211: """
212:     DEFAULT_OUTPUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
213:     DEFAULT_OUTPUT.write_text(module, encoding="utf-8")
214:     print(
215:         f"wrote {DEFAULT_OUTPUT.relative_to(REPO)}: {len(rows)} districts, "
216:         f"{points_total} points, {len(module)} bytes"
217:     )
218: 
219: 
220: if __name__ == "__main__":
221:     main()

44: # geoBoundaries spells nine city and direction units in English while
45: # data/tangerine/districts.csv spells them in Czech. Keyed by the
46: # normalized English form, mirroring ENGLISH_ALIASES in districtNames.ts.
47: ALIASES = {
48:     "prague": "praha",
49:     "prague east": "praha vychod",
50:     "prague west": "praha zapad",
51:     "plzen city": "plzen mesto",
52:     "plzen north": "plzen sever",
53:     "plzen south": "plzen jih",
54:     "brno city": "brno mesto",
55:     "brno country": "brno venkov",
56:     "ostrava city": "ostrava mesto",
57: }
58: 
59: CAPITAL_PREFIXES = {"hl", "hlavni", "mesto", "m"}
60: 
61: 
62: def rings_of(geometry: dict) -> list:
63:     """Every ring of a Polygon or MultiPolygon feature."""
64:     if geometry["type"] == "Polygon":
65:         return geometry["coordinates"]
66:     rings: list = []
67:     for polygon in geometry["coordinates"]:
68:         rings.extend(polygon)
69:     return rings
70: 
71: 
72: def project(lon: float, lat: float, lat0: float, lon0: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
73:     """Equirectangular with a cosine correction, y pointing down."""
74:     return ((lon - lon0) * math.cos(math.radians(lat0)), -lat)
75: 
76: 
77: def simplify(points: list, tolerance: float) -> list:
78:     """Iterative Douglas Peucker over a closed ring (first point repeated)."""
79:     if len(points) < 5:
80:         return points
81:     keep = [False] * len(points)
82:     keep[0] = keep[-1] = True
83:     stack = [(0, len(points) - 1)]
84:     tolerance_sq = tolerance * tolerance
85:     while stack:
86:         start, end = stack.pop()
87:         if end <= start + 1:
88:             continue
89:         ax, ay = points[start]
90:         bx, by = points[end]
91:         dx, dy = bx - ax, by - ay
92:         norm = dx * dx + dy * dy
93:         best = -1.0
94:         best_index = -1
95:         for index in range(start + 1, end):
96:             px, py = points[index]
97:             if norm == 0:
98:                 distance = (px - ax) ** 2 + (py - ay) ** 2
99:             else:
100:                 t = ((px - ax) * dx + (py - ay) * dy) / norm
101:                 t = 0.0 if t < 0 else (1.0 if t > 1 else t)
102:                 distance = (px - (ax + t * dx)) ** 2 + (py - (ay + t * dy)) ** 2
103:             if distance > best:
104:                 best = distance
105:                 best_index = index
106:         if best > tolerance_sq and best_index > 0:
107:             keep[best_index] = True
108:             stack.append((start, best_index))
109:             stack.append((best_index, end))
110:     return [point for point, flagged in zip(points, keep) if flagged]
111: 
112: 
113: def district_key(name: str) -> str:
114:     """The same join key src/lib/districtNames.ts produces."""
115:     plain = "".join(
116:         character
117:         for character in unicodedata.normalize("NFD", name)
118:         if not unicodedata.combining(character)
119:     )
120:     tokens = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", " ", plain.lower()).strip().split()
121:     start = 0
122:     while start < len(tokens) - 1 and tokens[start] in CAPITAL_PREFIXES:
123:         start += 1
124:     key = " ".join("nad" if token == "n" else token for token in tokens[start:])
125:     return ALIASES.get(key, key)
126: 
127: 
128: def main() -> None:
129:     document = json.loads(DEFAULT_INPUT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
130: 
131:     latitudes: list[float] = []
132:     longitudes: list[float] = []
133:     for feature in document["features"]:
134:         for ring in rings_of(feature["geometry"]):
135:             for lon, lat in ring:
136:                 longitudes.append(lon)
137:                 latitudes.append(lat)
138:     lat0 = (min(latitudes) + max(latitudes)) / 2
139:     lon0 = (min(longitudes) + max(longitudes)) / 2
140: 
141:     projected: list[tuple[str, list[list[tuple[float, float]]]]] = []
142:     for feature in document["features"]:
143:         shape: list[list[tuple[float, float]]] = []
144:         for ring in rings_of(feature["geometry"]):
145:             points = [project(lon, lat, lat0, lon0) for lon, lat in ring]
146:             points = simplify(points, TOLERANCE)
147:             if len(points) >= 4:
148:                 shape.append(points)
149:         projected.append((feature["properties"]["shapeName"], shape))
150: 
151:     xs = [x for _, shape in projected for ring in shape for x, _ in ring]
152:     ys = [y for _, shape in projected for ring in shape for _, y in ring]
153:     min_x, max_x = min(xs), max(xs)
154:     min_y, max_y = min(ys), max(ys)
155: 
156:     span_x = max_x - min_x
157:     span_y = max_y - min_y
158:     height = round(VIEW_WIDTH * span_y / span_x)
159:     scale = (VIEW_WIDTH - 2 * BORDER) / span_x
160: 
161:     def emit(ring: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> str:
162:         steps = [
163:             f"{round((x - min_x) * scale + BORDER)} {round((y - min_y) * scale + BORDER)}"
164:             for x, y in ring
165:         ]
166:         return "M" + "L".join(steps) + "Z"
167: 
168:     rows: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
169:     points_total = 0
170:     for name, shape in projected:
171:         path = "".join(emit(ring) for ring in shape)
172:         points_total += sum(len(ring) for ring in shape)
173:         rows.append((district_key(name), path))
174: 
175:     keys = [key for key, _ in rows]
176:     duplicates = sorted({key for key in keys if keys.count(key) > 1})
177:     if duplicates:
178:         raise SystemExit(f"duplicate normalized keys: {duplicates}")
179: 
180:     body = "\n".join(f"  {{ name: '{key}', path: '{path}' }}," for key, path in rows)
181:     module = f"""/**
182:  * Simplified district geometry for the cartogram map, written by
183:  * scripts/map/build_district_geometry.py from geoBoundaries gbOpen
184:  * CZE ADM2 (Public Domain, www.geoboundaries.org, 77 districts). The
185:  * outlines are projected to a flat map, simplified with Douglas
186:  * Peucker, and rounded onto a 1000 by {height} integer grid so the map
187:  * keeps the same chunky pixel edge the rest of the station wears.
188:  * Names are normalized keys, the same shape src/lib/districtNames.ts
189:  * produces, so the cartogram joins a districts.csv row to its outline
190:  * with no network at runtime.
191:  */
192: 
193: /** The viewBox every path in this file is drawn on. */
194: export const CZECHIA_VIEW_BOX = '0 0 1000 {height}'
195: 
196: /** One district outline under its normalized name. */
197: export interface DistrictGeometry {{
198:   /** Normalized district name, the join key. */
199:   name: string
200:   /** SVG path data on CZECHIA_VIEW_BOX. */
201:   path: string
202: }}
203: 
204: /** All 77 districts, one path each. */
205: export const CZECHIA_DISTRICTS: readonly DistrictGeometry[] = [
206: {body}
207: ]
208: 
209: /** Guard against a truncated or overgrown asset. */
210: export const CZECHIA_DISTRICT_COUNT = {len(rows)}
211: """
212:     DEFAULT_OUTPUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
213:     DEFAULT_OUTPUT.write_text(module, encoding="utf-8")
214:     print(
215:         f"wrote {DEFAULT_OUTPUT.relative_to(REPO)}: {len(rows)} districts, "
216:         f"{points_total} points, {len(module)} bytes"
217:     )
218: 
219: 
220: if __name__ == "__main__":
221:     main()
